description: The new early-return in `hotUpdate` guards on `!server?.hot` instead of `!server`, so it also bails out on dev servers that only expose the legacy `ws` channel, silently dropping the full-page reloads the code below still falls back to through `server.ws.send`.

The new regression test passes `modules: []`, which makes `isExternalFile` false so the handler returns before `server` is ever dereferenced — the test therefore passes even without the fix and does not actually cover the bundledDev crash.

In `readFromCss` the `Object.keys(obj).length === 1` condition was dropped from the DEFAULT shortcut, so a specific-key lookup on a namespace with more than one entry (e.g. `theme('colors.red')` when both `--color-red` and `--color-red-500` exist) now returns only the DEFAULT value instead of the full object.

kind: missing negation makes new branch dead code
description: In `resolveThemeValue` the relocated DEFAULT-unwrapping block requires `Array.isArray(resolvedValue)` (the `!` is missing), so the branch can never run and CSS `theme('…')` lookups that previously resolved to a namespace's DEFAULT value now resolve to nothing.
The Relations v2 adapter's lazy getter builds the relation keys from `db._?.schema` instead of `db._?.relations`, so v2 relation metadata is never read and joined queries lose their relation keys.

The v1 adapter's `getRelationKeysByModel` uses `??` instead of `??=`, so `relationKeysByModel` is never assigned and the relation-key map is rebuilt from `db._` on every joined query instead of being memoized once.

kind: wrong offset passed to the line-terminator probe
description: In `generateCodeFrame` the continuation-line branch probes the terminator at `count + lineLength` (a character in the middle of the following line) instead of at `count` (the terminator itself), so multi-line CRLF ranges undercount by one character per line and emit underlines of the wrong length.

In `posToNumber` the terminator length is probed at `lines[i].length` instead of the running `start` offset — identical only for the first line — so from the third line onward in a CRLF source the wrong character is inspected and the returned offset is short by one per CRLF line.

While adding QUERY to `req.fresh`, the rewritten guard drops `HEAD`, so HEAD requests no longer get conditional revalidation — a regression against the documented GET/HEAD behavior the PR only meant to extend.
original: if ('GET' !== method && 'HEAD' !== method && 'QUERY' !== method) return false;

kind: inverted condition in test skip guard
description: The first QUERY test's skip guard is inverted (`if (!shouldSkipQuery(...))`), so the test is skipped exactly on the Node versions that support QUERY and only runs on the ones that do not — note the sibling test below keeps the correct, non-inverted guard.

`createTeamForTeamPlanCustomer` calls `updateCustomerMetadata` without `await`, so the helper can return and the caller continue before Stripe's customer metadata is updated, and any failure surfaces as an unhandled rejection instead of an error.
original: await updateCustomerMetadata(customerId, { userId, teamId: team.id, type: 'TEAM' });

kind: wrong variable of a similar name
description: The new team-upgrade path in `synchronizeStripeWithJetstreamUserIfRequired` passes `teamId: userId` instead of `teamId: team.id`, so the just-created team's id is never used (leaving `team` unused) and the team sync runs against a user id.
